meta.description: Name pools per culture for random chargen naming. Expanded from Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3 (pp. 307–314); culture ids match data/core/cultures.json. Optional unisex_names for non-gendered traditions; naming_style and source_name_groups record appendix groupings.
source_books: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names pp. 307–314

middenrealm_cities.naming_style: Garethi/Middenrealm: given name plus family name, profession, origin, or noble 'von'.
middenrealm_cities.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

middenrealm_rural.naming_style: Garethi/Middenrealm: given name plus family name, profession, origin, or noble 'von'.
middenrealm_rural.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

andergast_nostria.naming_style: Andergastian and Nostrian: rustic, archaic first names; commoners often use origin or trade instead of true family names.
andergast_nostria.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

bornland.naming_style: Bornlandish: Garethi structure strongly influenced by Norbardic sound; serfs may lack family names.
bornland.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

svellt_valley_northern_lands.naming_style: Frontier mixture: Garethi/Bornlandish/Norbardic names, with orkish influence under occupation.
svellt_valley_northern_lands.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

almada.naming_style: Almadan: often three-part names with a Bosparanizing second name and melodious family name.
almada.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

horasian_empire.naming_style: Horathi: soft, melodious Bosparan-influenced names; noble particles can include ya, de, di, du, della.
horasian_empire.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

cyclops_islands.naming_style: Cyclopean: long, vowel-rich names with y, ph, ë, ï, ÿ; nobles may use 'a' plus origin and dyll/dylli lineage.
cyclops_islands.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

amazon_castle.naming_style: Garethi/Middenrealm: given name plus family name, profession, origin, or noble 'von'.
amazon_castle.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

arania.naming_style: Aranian: Tulamidian basis mixed with Garethi/Almadan forms.
arania.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

mhanadistan.naming_style: Tulamidian: given name plus patronymic/matronymic or honor-name; full names can be very formal.
mhanadistan.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

tulamidian_city_states.naming_style: Urban Tulamidian: given name plus lineage or honor-name; al'/el' honor names are common.
tulamidian_city_states.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

novadis_men.naming_style: Novadi male: given name, usually ibn plus father/teacher name; honor-names may replace normal lineage.
novadis_men.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

novadis_women.naming_style: Novadi female: given name, often bint plus father/teacher name; poetic honor-names exist.
novadis_women.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

ferkina.naming_style: Ferkina: hard Tulamidian-related names; men use iban, unmarried women sabu, married women zawsh(i); tribes often begin with Bân.
ferkina.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

zahori.naming_style: Zahori: Tulamidian, Almadan, Horasian, and fanciful mixed first names plus clan names.
zahori.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

thorwal.naming_style: Thorwalian: short two-syllable names, patronymic/matronymic -son/-dottir, or deed-name replacing lineage.
thorwal.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

gjalskerland.naming_style: Gjalsker: related to Hjalding/Thorwalian naming with clan, saga, and shamanic names.
gjalskerland.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

fjarninger.naming_style: Fjarninger: harsh northern names, often nickname-like and tied to ice, hunt, and strength.
fjarninger.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

jungle_tribes.naming_style: Forest People: non-gendered public names, often deed or quality names; secret Tapam names are not used publicly.
jungle_tribes.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

darna.naming_style: Forest People: non-gendered public names, often deed or quality names; secret Tapam names are not used publicly.
darna.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

lost_tribes.naming_style: Forest People: non-gendered public names, often deed or quality names; secret Tapam names are not used publicly.
lost_tribes.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

forest_island_utulus.naming_style: Utulu: rhythmic, usually non-gendered names; family names are generally not used.
forest_island_utulus.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

miniwatu.naming_style: Forest People: non-gendered public names, often deed or quality names; secret Tapam names are not used publicly.
miniwatu.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

tocamuyac.naming_style: Tocamuyac: short non-gendered island names; family names are generally not used.
tocamuyac.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

maraskan.naming_style: Maraskan: Garethi or Tulamidya roots extended with Maraskan suffixes; origin phrases are more common than true surnames.
maraskan.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

southern_aventuria.naming_style: Southern Aventurian/Brabaci: long, melodious names; multiple given names and family names are common.
southern_aventuria.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

buccaneers.naming_style: Buccaneer: mixed harbor names from Brabaci, Thorwalian, Tulamidian, and sailor nicknames.
buccaneers.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

nivesian_tribes.naming_style: Nivesian: given name plus herd, spirit, or reputation; close relation to reindeer-herding life.
nivesian_tribes.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

nuanaae_lie.naming_style: Nuanaä-Lie: Nivesian and elven naming influences; names may point to herd, spirit, song, or kinship.
nuanaae_lie.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

norbard_clan.naming_style: Norbardic: given name plus family/clan name; male and female forms are closely related.
norbard_clan.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

troll_peaks.naming_style: Troll Peaks/Kurga: dark, guttural names; honor or shame names can supplement or replace the given name.
troll_peaks.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

lea_elves.naming_style: Elvish/Isdira: first name plus a second name tied to kinship, soul animal, deed, or personal attribute; second names can change over life.
lea_elves.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

elven_settlement.naming_style: Elvish/Isdira: first name plus a second name tied to kinship, soul animal, deed, or personal attribute; second names can change over life.
elven_settlement.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

steppe_elven_clan.naming_style: Elvish/Isdira: first name plus a second name tied to kinship, soul animal, deed, or personal attribute; second names can change over life.
steppe_elven_clan.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

forest_elven_clan.naming_style: Elvish/Isdira: first name plus a second name tied to kinship, soul animal, deed, or personal attribute; second names can change over life.
forest_elven_clan.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

firn_elven_clan.naming_style: Elvish/Isdira: first name plus a second name tied to kinship, soul animal, deed, or personal attribute; second names can change over life.
firn_elven_clan.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

anvil_dwarves.naming_style: Dwarven/Rogolan: given name plus patronymic or matronymic using groscho/groschna; clan pride and alliteration matter.
anvil_dwarves.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

ore_dwarves.naming_style: Dwarven/Rogolan: given name plus patronymic or matronymic using groscho/groschna; clan pride and alliteration matter.
ore_dwarves.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

hill_dwarves.naming_style: Hill Dwarven: Rogolan names plus human-like family names from long contact with humans.
hill_dwarves.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

brilliant_dwarves.naming_style: Dwarven/Rogolan: given name plus patronymic or matronymic using groscho/groschna; clan pride and alliteration matter.
brilliant_dwarves.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

brobim.naming_style: Dwarven/Rogolan: given name plus patronymic or matronymic using groscho/groschna; clan pride and alliteration matter.
brobim.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

orkland.naming_style: Orkish: male given names; women are usually identified by physical features or owner/tribal relation. Heroic deed-names are rare.
orkland.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

yurach.naming_style: Yurach: ork names marked by exile, shame, or outsider status; deed-names can be bitter or hostile.
yurach.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

svellt_occupiers.naming_style: Svellt occupier orks: ork first names often combined with Middenrealm-style deed surnames.
svellt_occupiers.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

goblin_tribe.naming_style: Goblin: short guttural names; rare second names mark deeds. Festum goblins may use goblin-Bornlandish mixed names.
goblin_tribe.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

goblin_band.naming_style: Goblin: short guttural names; rare second names mark deeds. Festum goblins may use goblin-Bornlandish mixed names.
goblin_band.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

festum_ghetto.naming_style: Goblin: short guttural names; rare second names mark deeds. Festum goblins may use goblin-Bornlandish mixed names.
festum_ghetto.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

archaic_achaz.naming_style: Achaz/Rssahh: non-gendered names gained around the sixth shedding; earlier call-names may be based on traits or deeds.
archaic_achaz.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.

tribal_achaz.naming_style: Achaz/Rssahh: non-gendered names gained around the sixth shedding; earlier call-names may be based on traits or deeds.
tribal_achaz.source: Wege der Helden (2011), Appendix 3: Aventurian Names, pp. 307-314; expanded/adapted per culture.
